title: Blackened Salmon with Quinoa and Roasted Asparagus - High Protein Dinner
description: Enjoy a flavorful and filling dinner with this 25-minute recipe featuring spiced fish and wholesome grains. Each serving delivers 35 grams of protein to support your post-workout recovery. Save it for your next meal prep.

ingredients.note: avocado or canola oil, for the skillet

steps: In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed quinoa and chicken broth. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.

Place the trimmed asparagus on a baking sheet, toss with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and black pepper. Roast in the preheated oven at 400°F (200°C) for 12 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
In a small bowl, mix the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, dried thyme, remaining salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper to create the blackening spice blend.
Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels and coat the flesh side evenly with the spice blend.

Heat 1 tablespoon of high-heat oil (like avocado or canola oil) in a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Place the salmon fillets spice-side down in the skillet and cook for 4 minutes without moving until a dark crust forms.
Flip the salmon fillets and cook for an additional 3 to 4 minutes until the fish flakes easily with a fork and reaches an internal temperature of 145°F (63°C).
Divide the cooked quinoa, roasted asparagus, and blackened salmon among four plates and serve warm.
tips: Pat the salmon completely dry before adding the spices to ensure a proper dark crust forms in the skillet.
Store leftover cooked quinoa and salmon in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
You can substitute brown rice or cauliflower rice for the quinoa if desired.
storage: Store in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a skillet or microwave.

steps_short: Simmer the quinoa in chicken broth until fluffy.
Toss asparagus with oil and roast in the oven.
Coat salmon fillets evenly with the spice blend.
Sear the salmon in a hot skillet until crusted.
Serve the fish over warm quinoa with asparagus.

issues: Olive oil has a smoke point that is too low for traditional blackening; high-heat cooking oil (such as avocado or canola oil) should be used in the skillet.

The recipe calls for 1 tbsp of olive oil total with '1 teaspoon of olive oil' used for asparagus and 'remaining 2 teaspoons' used for the skillet, which mathematically sums to 1 tbsp, but the fat ratio for cooking 4 salmon fillets in a cast-iron skillet (2 tsp) is insufficient and will cause sticking and lack of proper searing crust.
